title: Venue profile
description: What the Venues page says about one venue: what it is, what it plays, who goes, how accessible it is and what it costs. Written by the venue profiler, one file per venue at data/venues/<id>.json. Every filled-in field must be named by an evidence item with a word-for-word quote. The written fields (summary, music.notes, crowd, cost.notes, accessibility.notes) are in our own words and may only say what their quotes say.

id.description: The venue's id in data/sources/<category>.json. The file name is <id>.json.

aliases.description: Other names the venue goes by (old names, how listings sites write it). Used to match listings to this venue.

types.description: What kind of place it is. Required for a venue that is not in data/sources/ (the registry's type list is used otherwise). Must be backed by a quote naming 'types'.

status.description: open (default) unless a source says otherwise. closed hides the venue from the Venues page; temporarily-closed and opening-soon are shown with a note.

location.description: Where the postcode is, from postcodes.io (scripts/zone.py). Required for a venue not in the registry; the zone must agree with distance_m.

distance_m.description: Straight-line metres from Bethnal Green tube.

discovered.description: Set when the weekly venue run found this venue. Keeps how and when.

website.description: The venue's own website, if it has one. Must be cited by an evidence item (fields: ['website']).

summary.description: One to three sentences, our own words: what kind of place it is and what it's known for. No adjectives the sources don't support, no promo language.

styles.description: Short lowercase music styles the sources name, e.g. ['indie', 'punk'] or ['house', 'techno']. Empty if not stated.

notes.description: Optional, our own words: the kind of nights or gigs it puts on.

crowd.description: Who goes, our own words, only as the sources describe it (e.g. how the venue describes itself, or a review). Null if nothing quotable. Never guess from the music or the area, and never describe people by age, race, class or looks unless a source says the venue is for that group (e.g. 'queer', '18+', 'families').

step_free.description: true only if a source says there is step-free access (or a lift/ramp to the main space); false only if a source says there isn't; otherwise null.

notes.description: Other access details the sources state (lifts, parts of the venue up or down stairs, access tickets, quiet spaces), our own words.

access_page.description: The venue's own access-information page, if it has one.

free_entry.description: 'always' if a source says entry is free; 'some-nights' if a source says some nights or some hours are free; 'no' if a source says there is always a charge; null if not stated. Prices on individual events come from our own listings, not from here.

notes.description: General pricing the sources state, our own words (e.g. a typical ticket range, membership, cash-only). Never a single event's price.

age_policy.description: As stated by a source, e.g. '18+ after 9pm'. Null if not stated.

capacity.description: Standing or total capacity a source states. Null if not stated.

story.description: The longer read under 'The story' on the venue page, written by the venue storyteller: when it opened, what has changed since, what it does now, what it is like inside, and other things a visitor would find interesting. Every part is our own words and backed by quotes naming it. Null until written.

opened.description: When it opened (or was built, or first became a venue), as a source states it, e.g. '1898, as a pub' or 'March 2019'.

then.description: Its history and what has changed since it opened (owners, names, rebuilds, closures and reopenings), our own words.

now.description: What it does now: its programme, regular nights, kitchen or projects, our own words, from sources no more than five years old.

vibe.description: What it is like inside, only as sources describe it (the room, the decor, the atmosphere), attributed where it is a judgement ('Time Out calls it...'). Never describes people by age, race, class or looks.

worth_knowing.description: Up to five short facts a visitor would find interesting (a famous gig, a listed building, a film shot there), our own words.

story_research.description: Internal bookkeeping for the venue storyteller, never shown on the site: when the story was last researched, what came of it, and when it may be tried again. A venue whose description is still under 15 lines is retried a week after last_attempt, never sooner.

outcome.description: written = the description now reaches 15 lines; partial = something was added but it is still short; nothing-found = nothing quotable was found.

next_check.description: The earliest date it may be researched again: last_attempt + 7 days unless the outcome is written (then null).

note.description: What was looked for and not found, for the next attempt.

review.description: The independent check of this profile: every quote re-fetched and every written field compared with its quotes. A review older than profiled_at doesn't count: the site waits for a fresh check after every change.

removed_fields.description: Fields emptied because they could not be confirmed.

needs_review.description: Set when something in the profile is in doubt. The site then shows only the registry basics for this venue.

history.description: What changed and who changed it, newest last. The venue editor and checker add a line each time they change the profile.

fields.description: Which profile fields this quote supports. Use the field name ('summary', 'crowd', 'website', 'age_policy', 'capacity', 'address', 'postcode') or a dotted name for parts ('music.styles', 'music.notes', 'accessibility.step_free', 'accessibility.accessible_toilet', 'accessibility.hearing_loop', 'accessibility.notes', 'accessibility.access_page', 'cost.free_entry', 'cost.notes'). 'music', 'accessibility' and 'cost' cover all their parts. Also 'types', 'status' (anything other than open) and 'aliases'. 'story' covers all of the story; or name its parts: 'story.opened', 'story.then', 'story.now', 'story.vibe', 'story.worth_knowing'.

quote.description: One contiguous snippet copied word for word from the page, 10 to 300 characters.

source_kind.description: primary = the venue's own website or its own page on a ticketing site; press = a review or article by a named publication; directory = an access guide or listings directory (AccessAble, Euan's Guide, CAMRA WhatPub, a council page); aggregator = a listings site that copies others.

source_date.description: When the page was written or last updated, if it shows a date. Needed on story evidence: a source over five years old may back story.opened and story.then (history) but not story.now or story.vibe.
